players.product: IBM Quantum Nighthawk (120 qubits, 218 tunable couplers) superconducting QPUs

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 results: CEO Arvind Krishna: revenue growth accelerated to 6% (constant currency), above the base case laid out in July, led by software growth of 9%, infrastructure growth of 5% and 'modest improvement in consulting'. CFO Jim Kavanaugh: consulting revenue grew 2%; 70 basis points of operating pre-tax margin expansion and 11% diluted operating earnings per share growth; adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 60 basis points; segment profit margins expanded 210 basis points in software and 120 basis points in infrastructure while consulting margin declined modestly on reinvestment; through the first nine months IBM generated about $8 billion of free cash flow, up 8% (about $600 million) year over year, the highest nine-month free cash flow margin in reported history. Software printed about $7.6 billion of revenue with over four points of organic growth; high-value annual recurring revenue grew 8% to $24.9 billion. Cash was $11.1 billion and debt $63.8 billion (including $12.7 billion for the financing business).
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue +6% (cc); software +9%, infrastructure +5%, consulting +2%; operating EPS +11%; 9-month free cash flow about $8 billion (+8%)

quarterly_data.signal: Software detail (CEO Arvind Krishna, CFO Jim Kavanaugh): Red Hat revenue grew 11% with bookings accelerating back to the high teens; OpenShift is a $2.4 billion ARR business growing more than 30%; virtualization has nearly $800 million in contracts signed since early 2024 and about $750 million in pipeline. Data grew 20% (Confluent bookings growth of about 20%); transaction processing grew 10%, which management says shows the second-quarter softness was timing rather than demand; HashiCorp grew bookings across all geographies, while automation faced a tougher compare. The transactional 20% of software grew double digits, led by enterprise license agreements up north of 20% with net revenue retention north of 130%. Of the roughly $400 million of large deals that slipped from Q2, IBM closed about two-thirds ($250-plus million), about a quarter of the software acceleration, with about three-quarters from net new business. CEO: 'I do not expect double-digit performance in TP to keep going' and expects a moderation into the fourth quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: Red Hat +11%; OpenShift ARR $2.4 billion (>30%); Data +20%; TP +10%; slipped deals ~$400 million, two-thirds closed

quarterly_data.signal: Infrastructure and IBM Z (CEO Arvind Krishna, CFO Jim Kavanaugh): distributed infrastructure grew 32% and storage delivered record revenue growth and gained share (FlashSystem, Storage Fusion, Tape, IBM Z storage); CEO: 'AI continues to increase demand for storage'. z17 generated more than $1 billion of incremental revenue over six quarters compared with prior programs and is at 125% program to date, the highest recorded; the new single-frame and rack-mount IBM Z systems introduced in July gave the strongest mid-range IBM Z launch in nearly two decades. Installed MIPS are up high teens (18%) six quarters in and shipped MIPS up over 100%; IBM runs 145 million MIPS worldwide; clients representing approximately 85% of installed MIPS capacity are maintaining or growing capacity. CFO: every dollar landed on mainframe brings $3-$5 of software; mainframe runs 70% of the industry's transaction volumes in terms of value, including 45 of the top 50 banks. IBM Z delivers a two to 15 times total cost of ownership advantage versus off-platform alternatives (CEO).
quarterly_data.figure: distributed infrastructure +32%; z17 >$1 billion incremental revenue over six quarters; installed MIPS +18%, shipped MIPS >100%

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog and pipeline (CFO Jim Kavanaugh, CEO Arvind Krishna): IBM exited the quarter 'with a sizable backlog in distributed infrastructure' and is well positioned for continued momentum in Q4. AI represented about 30% of consulting revenue in the quarter and 35% of the consulting backlog; consulting strategy and technology grew 4%. Lightwell (remediated open-source packages) is now generally available; some of the world's largest enterprises signed up and its pipeline is approaching $700 million, with more than 40,000 remediated packages released to the Lightwell network.
quarterly_data.figure: AI 35% of consulting backlog; Lightwell pipeline approaching $700 million

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook (CFO Jim Kavanaugh): IBM continues to expect 2026 revenue growth of 4%-5% and raises its free cash flow growth expectation to more than $1 billion; profit and free cash flow stay anchored to the 4% base case. Full-year software growth now approximately 7%-8%, with about 7% as the revised base case (hybrid cloud double-digit, data mid-teens, automation low double-digit, transaction processing raised to flat); consulting low to mid-single-digit growth; 100 basis points of operating pre-tax margin expansion; operating tax rate in the mid-teens; free cash flow realization of about 130%. CFO: 'We feel comfortable with that $32 billion of revenue' in software for the year, and high-value recurring revenue should approach double-digit growth in Q4. CEO Arvind Krishna: 'comfortable about double-digit growth in the fourth quarter' for Red Hat; IBM will quantify 2027 in January.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue growth 4%-5%; free cash flow growth more than $1 billion (raised); software approximately 7%-8%

quarterly_data.signal: Quantum (CEO Arvind Krishna): in July three independent demonstrations of quantum advantage were achieved on IBM hardware with the University of Chicago, Algorithmiq and Qedma; the Nighthawk r2 processor delivers 7,500 gates, executes 100,000 circuits per second and enables performance improvements of up to 19 times over prior-generation systems (CEO: workloads costing approximately $100 to run on IBM could cost up to $10 million on slower competitive modalities). IBM was selected for Stage C, the third phase of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative. IBM Quantum signed 16 enterprise engagements this year across automotive, aerospace, telecommunications, financial services and manufacturing, including AT&T and General Motors, now part of the IBM Quantum Network. IBM connected its first modular cryogenic systems, continues work on its 300,000 sq ft Poughkeepsie manufacturing facility, and closed the $1 billion award from the Department of Commerce in Anderon for manufacturing quantum wafers; the CEO says that after the Starling demonstration IBM is 'ready to scale'.
quarterly_data.figure: Nighthawk r2 7,500 gates, 100,000 circuits per second, up to 19x; 16 enterprise engagements; $1 billion Department of Commerce award closed

quarterly_data.signal: AI platforms (CEO Arvind Krishna): llm-d, an open-source project developed with Red Hat and Google, reuses previously processed context to help clients run large AI models at five to 10 times lower cost on existing GPU infrastructure; IBM Bob now runs on-prem; HashiCorp Vault registers, authorizes, audits and revokes agents, and IBM Agent Identity and HashiCorp Vault are partnering with NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform; Apptio now connects AI spend and token consumption to business results. Confluent's Streamhouse capability (real-time data capture, transformation and query) is to be announced 'in a couple of weeks' as a cross-sell on top of Confluent. CFO Jim Kavanaugh: IBM Consulting has new strategic partnerships with OpenAI and an expanded relationship with Google Cloud.
quarterly_data.figure: llm-d five to 10 times lower cost

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Arvind Krishna's views on enterprise AI: sovereign AI 'is now beginning to pick up' in 2026, driving 'a big boom in AI infrastructure on-premise' that IBM's mainframe with Spyre cards will also benefit from, and a boom behind open-weight models; he computes that an average large enterprise can get going with 'maybe two or three racks' to run open-weight models at 'anywhere from 25% to 10% of the token cost of the frontier models', now about '90% as effective'. Enterprises are becoming more cognizant of the true ROI of AI spend and picking partners to redesign workflows, a tailwind for OpenShift, Confluent and mainframe. CFO Jim Kavanaugh: IBM drove 500 basis points of gross productivity in Q3 and is now north of $5.5 billion of productivity.
quarterly_data.figure: open-weight models 25% to 10% of frontier token cost; two or three racks; productivity north of $5.5 billion
